perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s available perspective:

- He is Harold Padilla, a project manager. He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer, friend, and trusted advisor he often turns to for advice and support.
- He felt frustrated and anxious about his project’s progress and believed his team was not performing well because they lacked motivation. He arranged to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- At that meeting, Harold told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and it was affecting progress. He heard Arthur say motivation can be tricky, ask whether Harold had tried understanding what drives each member individually, and suggest one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood personally. Harold agreed, said he would try it, thanked Arthur, and felt hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He believed Arthur’s advice would help and decided to implement it.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposed quick one-on-one chats to understand each member’s motivation. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and urged the team to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future and decided to discuss alternative strategies with Arthur again.
- In their second conversation, Harold told Arthur the suggestions had not worked and he was worried. He heard Arthur say there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold said he would set up another round of meetings and thanked Arthur.
- Harold became determined and focused. He believed there might be underlying team issues he had not addressed and decided to investigate the team’s dynamics through one-on-one meetings.
- In those meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension between a few team members affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed. Harold said he understood, would consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He believed addressing individual concerns would improve performance and intended to create a more supportive, open team environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- At another team meeting, Harold announced regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help them work better together, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad, urged the team to work together, and said their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

He does not have access to Arthur’s private thoughts, the team members’ unspoken issues, or any narrator-only assessments beyond what he himself experienced, was told, observed, or did.
